subject: Sustained completion delays & mitigation plan for Novonow
messages:
From: Thomas Li <thomas.li@novonow.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@novonow.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Apr 2024 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Noticeable spike in completion delays this week

Ben —

We're seeing a sustained set of slower completions across our traffic starting Monday evening. P95 looks OK but a non-trivial fraction of requests are taking 6–12x the median and a subset are timing out. Error rate is creeping up (0.6% -> 1.8%) and throughput throttles aren't letting us recover. I've attached a sample set of request traces and a topology diagram.

We're on a committed tier (contract NW-5231) and this is impacting a checkout flow for several stores. Can you confirm receipt and advise next steps? We need an ETA on mitigation and whether you can temporarily prioritize our traffic.

Thanks,
Thomas Li
Head of Platform, Novonow
thomas.li@novonow.com

Attachments: request-traces-20240424.ndjson, service-topology.png

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Thomas Li <thomas.li@novonow.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Apr 2024 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Noticeable spike in completion delays this week

Thomas —

Thanks for the traces and topology — I got them. I'm very sorry for the impact. I'm looping in Sofia (Customer Success) and Karthik (Infra) to investigate. Initial ask: can you confirm the time window where you see the worst tail (start/end UTC) and whether you can share any request ids that timed out?

Immediate next steps from our side:
- Karthik will triage traces and check queue/backpressure metrics and per-pool concurrency caps.
- We'll evaluate a short-term prioritization (routing policy) and a temporary cap bump if safe.
- I'll schedule a 1-hour bridge for tomorrow morning (propose 08:00 PDT) for triage and customer-facing comms.

I'll update here in 30–45 minutes with our triage findings.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Thomas Li <thomas.li@novonow.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 24 Apr 2024 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Noticeable spike in completion delays this week

Ben / Thomas —

I pulled the traces and correlated them with our serving telemetry. Initial observations:
- There's a clear buildup in per-shard request queues around 20:30–23:00 UTC on 2024-04-23 and recurring 01:00–04:00 UTC on 2024-04-24 (matches the traces).
- When queue depth exceeds ~750/slice we hit an internal concurrency cap that stops new allocations; requests are queued and KV cache misses increase, amplifying latency.
- A batching policy change upstream increased average batch size for the model family Novonow is pinned to; larger batches + CPU-side preprocessing variance appears to be widening the service time distribution, which triggers backpressure.

Short-term mitigations I can enact right now (low risk):
1) Increase concurrency cap for Novonow's pool by 20% (temp) and drain queues — should lower the long tail in 2–5 minutes.
2) Apply a soft-priority flag on the routing layer so their requests preempt lower-tier background jobs for 60 minutes.
3) Reduce batching max-window for the pinned model to force smaller, more predictable batches (will cost a small throughput drop).

I recommend doing 1 + 2 immediately, and 3 as a fallback if tail persists. I'll produce an ops runbook snippet and attach a small archive of the matched traces.

I attached sample-traces.zip.

Karthik
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Attachment: sample-traces.zip

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Thomas Li <thomas.li@novonow.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Apr 2024 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Noticeable spike in completion delays this week

Thomas —

Thanks for raising this and for your patience. We ran the immediate mitigations Karthik suggested (concurrency cap bump + soft-priority routing) at 08:50 UTC this morning. Early telemetry shows a reduction in the 99th percentile tail from ~2.8s to ~1.1s for the slices you provided; error rate trend is moving down as well. We'll continue to monitor for 24 hours.

Customer-facing play:
- We'll host a 60-minute bridge at 08:00 PDT tomorrow (agenda: what happened, mitigation applied, next permanent fixes).
- If the tail resurfaces we'll propose rolling a quantization/quantization-profile change for the pinned model and a controlled decrease in batch max-window.
- As a gesture for the impact we'll offer a one-time credit equivalent to two days of committed usage (pending Marissa's sign-off).

Can you confirm the bridge time works and whether you'd like any execs from your side on the call?

Sofia Ivanova
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Thomas Li <thomas.li@novonow.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 26 Apr 2024 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Noticeable spike in completion delays this week

Thomas / team —

Quick executive summary and next steps:
- Impact: sustained long-tail completions affecting Novonow checkout; peak error rate 1.8%; incident window Apr 23 20:30 UTC -> Apr 24 04:30 UTC (recurring patterns).
- Immediate: Karthik applied a 20% concurrency cap bump + soft-priority routing at 08:50 UTC 04/25; observed p99 improvement and error rate reduction.
- Next 24h: monitoring and a guide for a controlled change to batching policy (target: reduce max batch window by 40%). Karthik will prepare a minimal-risk rollout plan.
- Customer comms: 60-minute bridge scheduled 08:00 PDT tomorrow; Sofia will lead.
- Commercial: offering a one-time credit (2 days) subject to Marissa's approval.

Marissa — can you confirm approval for the credit and whether product/infra leadership want an exec readout tonight? If yes, I'll pull a 15-minute slot.

Thomas — appreciate the fast collaboration here. We will share the runbook and a short incident report after 24 hours of stable telemetry.

Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
